name: Dependency Audit
description: Enforces checking dependencies for known vulnerabilities before adding and during CI builds.
content:
# Dependency Audit Rules

- Run `npm audit`, `pip audit`, `bundle audit`, or equivalent before adding any new dependency
- Block merges with critical or high severity vulnerabilities — configure `npm audit --audit-level=high` in CI
- Use Dependabot, Renovate, or Snyk to automatically create PRs for vulnerable dependency updates
- Pin dependency versions in lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `Pipfile.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`) — never rely on floating ranges in production
- Evaluate new dependencies before adding — check download count, maintenance activity, open issues, and known CVEs
- Prefer well-maintained dependencies with small dependency trees — fewer transitive dependencies means less attack surface
- Review dependency licenses — ensure compatibility with your project's license, block copyleft licenses if needed
- Use socket.dev or npm-audit-resolver to detect supply chain attacks — typosquatting, malicious postinstall scripts
- Set up automated alerts for new CVEs affecting your dependency tree — don't wait for scheduled scans
- Keep the dependency count minimal — evaluate whether you truly need a package or can implement the functionality in a few lines
- Run `npm ls --all` or equivalent to audit the full transitive dependency tree periodically
- Document approved dependencies in an allowlist for security-sensitive projects — new dependencies require security review
